newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas slips in West, rises in East.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas slips in West, rises in East.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices on Tuesday softened in the West but firmed in the East with the lingering heat and NYMEX uptick, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was discussed at C$1.54-1.55 per gigajoule, down three cents from Monday.
August AECO was quoted around C$1.50, while one-year pricing eased to C$1.70-1.71, traders said.
A maintenance outage on NOVA Gas Transmission's Grande Prairie mainline in northern Alberta, which began Sunday, is taking about about one billion cubic feet per day off the system through Thursday.
However, most traders agreed that the outage was having little effect on the market since it was scheduled.
In response to the softer Alberta market, Sumas prices eased two cents to the low-$1.20s per million British thermal units, traders said.
At Niagara, prices were quoted three cents higher in the mid-to-high $2.30s per mmBtu as temperature highs in Toronto hovered in the mid-80s degrees F.
Also helping to lift the market higher, traders said, was the uptick on NYMEX. August Henry Hub gas futures rose to a high of $2.185 earlier in the session, up 3.4 cents from Monday.
